en: Resembling the rising sun, possessing noble strength of arm and prowess,
with the beauty of ten million Cupids, and proficient in all branches of knowledge.
I meditate upon the son of the Wind-god, who delights the heart of Śrī Rāma, who is a wish-fulfilling tree for his devotees, and who grants fearlessness and boons with his two arms.

Now begins the hymn of a thousand names: Hanumān, the bestower of prosperity, the son of Vāyu, Rudra, the sinless, the ageless, the immortal, the hero among heroes, the dweller in the village, and the refuge of people. (1)
Bestower of wealth, devoid of worldly qualities, heroic, valiant, lord of treasures, sage, tawny-eyed, granter of boons, eloquent, and destroyer of Sītā’s grief. ||2||
Śiva, Śarva, the Supreme, the Unmanifest, the Manifest-Unmanifest, the Supporter of the Earth; he with tawny hair and tawny body-hair, who is accessible through the Vedas, the Eternal One. ||3||
The Lord God is beginningless, the cause of the universe, and without support; he is the healer, the Lord of the universe, the Protector of the universe, and the Sovereign of Hari. ||4||
Bharga, Rāma, the devotee of Rāma, Kalyāṇa, he who is firm in his nature; Viśvaṃbhara, Viśvamūrti, Viśvākāra, and Viśvapā. ||5||

The soul of the universe, served by the universe, the universe itself, the sun that withdraws the universe; the activator of the universe, accessible to the universe, the one to be meditated upon by the universe, the bearer of all arts. ||6||
The monkey, the best of apes, knowable through the Vedas, the forest-dweller; the child, the old man, the youth, the reality, accessible through reality, indeed blissful and unborn.
The son of Anjanā, known in the village as Dharādhara, was composed; he was the imperishable Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Maharloka, Janoloka, and Tapoloka. 8.
He is Truth, the goal of the syllable Om, the all-pervading and stainless Praṇava; He is Śiva, the establisher of Dharma, beloved by Rāma and dear to Arjuna. ||9||

He who has turned the lord of waters into mere hoofprints for his cattle, whose desires are fulfilled, the lord of the earth, the slayer of demons, the lotus-eyed one, who is affectionate toward those who seek refuge. ||10||
The giver of life to Jānakī and the taker of the life of the Rākṣasa; full of perfect courage, clad in yellow garments, and possessing a splendor equal to the sun. ||11||
The remover of Droṇa, the wielder of the spear, the killer of the Rākṣasa Śakti, the destroyer of Akṣa, the messenger of Rāma, and the taker of the life-force of the Śākinīs. ||12||

He who utters the sound "bhu," the destroyer of enemies, the crusher of the pride of the wicked, the cause and the possessor of causes, the pure one, the sustainer of the universe, and the teacher of the world. ||13||
The protector of the world, the lord of the world, the master of the world, the sovereign of men; the father of the world, Hari, the Lord of Śrī, the destroyer of Garuḍa’s pride. ||14||

The banner of Pārtha has the son of Vāyu as its crest; it has immeasurable tails and immeasurable radiance. Its tail is Brahman, its supreme tail is the Supreme Brahman, and it is indeed beloved by Rāma. ||15||
Accompanied by Sugrīva and others, the wise lord of monkeys is a long-lived one who endures for an eon; he is ever-gracious and eternally auspicious. ||16||

He is the humble one, the one of noble course, the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, and the giver of fame; he is fame itself, the granter of fame, the ocean, the bestower of prosperity, and the auspicious one. ||17||
The God who traverses the ocean, the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra, the binder of the waters, the conqueror of the universe, and the one established in the universe. ||18||
The ornament of Laṅkā, the personification of Time, the destroyer of the home of the Lord of Laṅkā; the abode of all beings, Vāsudeva, Vasu, the Lord of the three worlds. ||19||
Śrī Rāma’s messenger Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of the palaces of Laṅkā; Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, who is praised, the peaceful one, the giver of peace, and the purifier of the universe. 20.

The enjoyer of the universe, the slayer of Māra, the celibate student who has conquered his senses; he who moves upward, the one with a tail, the one wearing a garland, and the one who slew the Rākṣasa with his tail. ||21||
The heroic son of Samīra is Vīramāra, the bestower of victory; he is the merit-bestowing giver of auspiciousness to the world, whose hearing and chanting are meritorious. ||22||
He is of meritorious fame, the one whose path is merit, the purifier of the world and the purifier itself; he is the Lord of Gods, the conqueror of Māra, and the bestower of devotion to Rāma. ||23||

He is the meditator, the object of meditation, fortune, and the witness; he is consciousness itself, whose very form is pure awareness. He is the giver of knowledge and the giver of life; he is the vital breath, the life-force of the universe, and the wind. (24)
The beloved of Vibhīṣaṇa, the hero, the bestower of perfection upon Pippalāyana; the friend, the refuge of the Siddhas, Time, and the destroyer of the devourer of Time. ||25||

He is the slayer of the Lord of Laṅkā, the one who dwells there, the sovereign who burns Laṅkā; he has the moon, sun, and fire as his eyes, and is the fire of time that brings an end to the dissolution.
Kapila, lord of monkeys, heap of merit, residing in the twelve zodiac signs; the refuge of all, immeasurable self, the warder-off of Revatī and others. ||27||
He is the giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa, the cause of Sītā’s existence, the object of Rāma’s meditation, Hṛṣīkeśa, a devotee of Viṣṇu, matted-haired, and powerful. (28)

The destroyer of the pride of the enemies of the gods, the invoker, the creator, the destroyer, the Lord of the universe, the protector of cities and villages, pure, awakened, and without interval. ||29||
Stainless, free from conceptual construction, transcending the qualities (guṇas), and formidable; Hanumān is difficult to propitiate, while Maheśvara is to be attained through austerity. ||30||

He who removes the torment arising from Janakī’s profound grief, who is higher than the highest, who transcends speech and mind, whose nature is both being and non-being, and who is beyond primordial nature (prakṛti). ||31||
The bestower of fortune, the stainless leader, the burner of Laṅkā; the Yātudhāna bound by the tail, the one dear to the enemies of the Yātudhānas. ||32||
The Lord of Beings who removes fatigue, the Lord of the World who bestows the true goal, the Lord of Monkeys, Wrath himself, whose eyes are bloodshot with anger. (33)

He is the remover of anger, the remover of suffering, the bestower of fearlessness and boons upon his devotees; he is compassionate toward his devotees, the Lord of the Universe, invoked by many, and the destroyer of cities.
Agni, Vibhāvasu, Bhāsvat, Yama, and Niṣkṛti; Varuṇa, Vāyugati, Vāyu, Kaubera, and Īśvara. ||35||
The Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu; the Wind, the Creator, the Sustainer, the Destroyer, and the one born of the Wind. (36)

The enemy of the enemies of the gods who has reduced them to the state of mosquitoes; the slayer of Madhu; desire itself; the monkey; the protector of desire; the tawny one; the life of the universe. ||37||

He whose lotus feet are the Bhāgīrathī; he who is skilled in the construction of the bridge; he who is Svāhā, Svadhā, the oblation for the gods, and the oblation for the ancestors; and he who is the illuminator of the bearer of sacrificial offerings.
Self-luminous, the great hero, light, and of immeasurable valor; possessing the movements of gliding and soaring, the true goal, the Supreme Person (Puruṣottama). ||39||
He is the soul of the universe, the womb of the universe, and indeed the end of the universe; he is infinite, free from sin, stainless, great, and the source of pride and ego.

He is space, wind, earth, water, fire, and the guardian of the quarters; he is the knower of the field (kṣetrajña), the protector of the field (kṣetrapāla), and one who has turned the ocean into a mere puddle. ||41||
He is golden-hued and ancient, moving through the sky and moving upon the earth; he is Manu, Hiraṇyagarbha, Sūtrātman, the king of kings, and the lord of the people. 42.

He who is to be known through Vedānta, the Udgītha, the one who has mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences (Vedāṅgas), who dwells in every village, who is to be attained, the bestower of spiritual manifestation, and a mine of virtues. (43)
He is garlanded with stars, the soul of all beings, fragrant, the wish-fulfilling tree, the thought-gem, the treasury of virtues, the lord of creatures, and unsurpassed.
The Lord of the City, of glorious fame, the radiant lord of the night, terrified the pretas, bhūtas, and piśācas with his shouts of "kili-kili."

He is the destroyer of the three Vedas, the subtle, the gross, the all-pervading, and the Supreme Person; he is the remover of epilepsy, the rememberer, the sacred tradition, the song, the memory, and the law-giver Manu. 46.
The Lord of Monkeys is the door to heaven, the door to progeny, and the door to liberation; he is the Supreme Brahman in the form of Sound, the ancient Brahman of Brahman. ||47||
He is one, not many; he is pure, self-luminous, and free from agitation; he is light, the primordial light, sattvic, and the best among those characterized by passion (rājas). ||48||
The remover of darkness, the supportless, the formless, the mine of virtues; the locus of qualities, composed of qualities, of vast body, and of great fame. ||49||
He has a large bow, large feet, a large head, and a loud voice; he has large ears, a large nose, large eyes, and a large neck.
He has a large body, great activity, a large tail, and large hands; he possesses a vast gait, is worthy of great service, and bestows the fruits of the great worlds. 51.
Possessing great power, possessing great desire, the bestower of great fruit, the Great Lord, praised by the great world, the Seer, the giver of knowledge, the Teacher of the Universe. ||52||
The preceptor of the gods, a speaker of truth, a proponent of the Veda, and a master of the arts; one who can travel to the seven netherworlds and who dwells upon the Malaya mountain. ||53||
Abiding in the northern quarter, the bestower of prosperity, master of divine herbs, the bird, the monkey, the lord of apes, ancient, and moving through the Vedas. (54)
The Brahmin is the fourfold one, the yogi who is to be reached through yoga, beyond the highest; he is without beginning or end, the all-pervading Vyāsa, Vaikuṇṭha, and the Lord of the Earth. ||55||

The vanquisher of enemies who has conquered them, the eternally blissful Lord; the protector of the earth, the lord of cattle, the guardian; the dark age, time itself, and that which is higher than the highest. ||56||
The yogi whose speed is always mental destroys the fear of saṃsāra; he is the giver of reality, the knower of reality, reality itself, and the illuminator of reality. ||57||

He is pure, awakened, eternally liberated, the king of devotees, the bestower of victory; he is the dissolution, possessed of immeasurable illusion, yet transcending illusion and free from envy. ||58||
He is the protection won through illusion, the world created by illusion, the refuge of illusion, untainted, the deceiver of illusion, and blissful.
The Naga is blissful and the bestower of bliss; he is praised by Maheśa. He is Maheśvara, true to his promise, Śarabha, and the purifier of the Kali age. ||60||

Bhairava is taste and the knower of taste, the mind and the eye of austerity; he is the sense of smell and fragrance, the organ of touch and tangibility, and the bestower of the pride of ego-consciousness.
He who is to be approached as "not thus, not thus," the beloved of devotion, Vaikuṇṭha; the Lord of the Mountain, the consort of Girijā, Dūrvāsas, the poet, and Aṅgiras. ||62||
Bhṛgu, Vasiṣṭha, Yavana, Tumburu, the stainless Nārada, the field of the universe, the seed of the universe, the eye of the universe, and he who moves throughout the universe. 63.
The sacrificer, the patron of the sacrifice, the purifier, and likewise the ancestors; faith, intellect, forgiveness, lassitude, the mantra, that which is joined with the mantra, and the tone. ||64||

The lord of kings, the sovereign, adorned with a garland of skulls, the charioteer of the world; he is eternal, his desires are ever-fulfilled, and he is the supreme granter of the wishes of his devotees. ||65||
The leader of the hosts, the lord of monkeys, the brother, the father, and the mother of Māruti; he is the Puruṣa with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet.

The conqueror of desire, the burner of desire, desire itself, and the bestower of desirable fruits; the taker of the *mudrā*, the slayer of *rākṣasas*, the remover of the earth’s burden, and the powerful one. ||67||
He who fights with claws and teeth, the devotee of Viṣṇu, the bestower of the boon of fearlessness, the destroyer of pride, the giver of pride, the haughty one, the hundred-formed, and the formless.

The great treasure, the one of great enjoyment, the one of great fortune, the giver of great wealth; the one of great form, the great yogi, the one of great splendor, the one of great radiance. ||69||
He is of great action, great sound, great mantra, and great intelligence; he is of great disposition, most generous, the pervasive lord whose essence is Mahādeva. (70)
Rudrakarman, Kṛtakarman, Ratnanābha, Kṛtāgama, Ambhodhilaṅghana, Siṃha, Nitya, Dharma, and Pramodana. ||71||

The conqueror of enemies, victory itself, equal victory, he whose vehicle is the wind; the giver of life, the thousand-rayed sun, the deliverer from death, and the one who bestows abundant sacrificial fees.

Siddhārtha, the bestower of success, whose resolve is perfected, the cause of accomplishment; he whose feet traverse the seven netherworlds, and who is worshipped by the host of the seven sages. ||73||
The hero who has crossed the seven oceans, whose vast domain consists of the seven continents, who bestows the happiness of the seven-limbed kingdom, and who is attended by the seven mothers. (74)

He is the sole crown of the seven worlds, the seven officiating priests, and the refuge of the seven musical notes; he is the treasury of the seven meters, the seven meters themselves, and the support of the seven classes of beings.
He is sung of by the seven Sāmans, he is the refuge of the seven underworlds; he is the wise one, the bestower of fame, the remover of grief, and the destroyer of misfortune.
It brings everything under control, destroys defects of the womb, and bestows sons and grandsons; it paralyzes the mouths of adversaries, gladdens the heart, and bestows grace. (77)
He is the pacifier of hostile sorcery, the destroyer of suffering, and the bestower of liberation from bondage; he is the support of the city of nine gates and his abode is within those nine gates.

Praiseworthy as Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the lord of men, the Great Lord (Maheśvara), girt with a belt, clad in armor, bearing a sword, resplendent, and the charioteer of the Victorious One (Arjuna). ||79||
His tail is many yojanas in width; with his tail he struck down asuras, and he is the slayer of malevolent planets and the destroyer of piśāca-grahas. ||80||
He is the destroyer of the Bāla-grahas, the leader of Dharma, and the bestower of compassion; he is of fierce deeds, fierce impetus, and fierce eyes, and is the performer of a hundred sacrifices.

Praised by Śatamanyu, he is the one to be praised, praise itself, and the praiser; he possesses great strength, is endowed with all virtues, is ever-active, and is the destroyer of the Rākṣasas. ||82||

The slayer of Rākṣasas with his hand, the Lord of Brahmā, the bearer of Śrī, the one who is affectionate toward his devotees; he whose roar is like a cloud, who has the form of a cloud, and who wards off the downpour of rain. ||83||
Megha is the cause of life, Megha is dark-hued and the supreme self; he is the son of Samīra, awakened, and proficient in the knowledge of reality. ||84||
Amogha, Amoghahṛṣṭi, Bestower of Desires, Destroyer of the Undesirable, the Purpose, Remover of Misfortune, the Competent One—such is the servant of Rāma. ||85||
The seeker of truth, the blessed one, the enemy of the Asuras, the lotus-eyed one, the self-born, Saṃkarṣaṇa, the pure-souled one, the mass of knowledge, and the lord of the gods. ||86||
The immovable one, the uprooter, the eternal, the builder of the bridge, Rāma, the charioteer; bliss, supreme bliss, the fish, the tortoise, the treasure, and tranquility.
Vārāha, Nārasiṃha, Vāmana, Jamadagnija, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Śiva, Buddha, Kalkī, and Hara who takes refuge in Rāma. ||88||
Nandi, Bhṛṅgi, Caṇḍī, and Gaṇeśa who is served by the Gaṇas; the presiding lord of karma, the presiding lord of the gods, the place of rest, and the Lord of the worlds. (89)
Jagannātha, the best of monkeys, the dweller in all, the eternal refuge, praised by Sugrīva and others, the peaceful one, the performer of all deeds, the leaper. ||90||
And there were Rākṣasas who tore with their claws, experts in wrestling with claws; also Kuśala, Sughana, Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, and Svara.
Golden-hued and endowed with strength, Rama is worthy of worship and the destroyer of sins; he is the lamp of liberation, liberation itself, Garuḍa, the serpent, and the Guru. ||92||

One who has destroyed the pride of enemies by the sound of his laughter, the shatterer of mountains; he whose limbs are adamantine, whose speed is adamantine, the devotee, and the warder-off of the adamantine. ||93||

Nakhāyudha (Claw-Weaponed), Maṇigrīva (Jewel-Necked), Jvālāmālī (Garlanded with Flames), Bhāskara (the Sun), Prauḍhapratāpa (of Mature Splendor), Tapanas (the Scorcher), and Bhaktatāpanivāraka (the Dispeller of Devotees' Suffering). ||94||

He is the refuge, the life-force, and the enjoyer; he possesses diverse activities yet is truly unshakable. He is perfectly healthy, the destroyer of ill-health, and the pacifier of suffering—the son of the Wind-god. 95.
The purifier, the wind, the beloved, the one who forgives the offenses of his devotees, the powerful one; the enemy of Meghanāda, the destroyer of the Rākṣasa Meghanāda. ||96||
The perishable and the imperishable, the self-disciplined one, the lord of monkeys, the refuge of the virtuous; Śrīkaṇṭha and Śitikaṇṭha, the companion and the leader. ||97||

He is without grossness and without atomicity; he is the divine splendor that destroys the cycle of rebirth. He is the essence of the science of the supreme self, skilled in the supreme self, and possessed of sublime intelligence. ||98||
He is stainless, the cause of truth, moving in truth, having truth as his sphere of activity; he has truth as his womb, truth as his form, he is truth itself, and his prowess is truth. ||99||

Añjanā, the vital breath (prāṇa), the liṅga, and the auspicious Vāyu born of the lineage; he who possesses a beautiful form, the form of Rudra, the one of excellent form, and the bearer of variegated forms. ||100||
He who is saluted by Maināka, the subtle-seer, the victorious, the conqueror, who has traversed the circle of the quarters, the Rudra who has manifested his prowess. ||101||
With a neck like a conch, a serene soul, a short nose, and a large belly; with protruding lips, wearing earrings and a variegated garland—he was the foremost among those who know yoga. ||102||
Vipaścit was a wise sage whose very form was bliss, who followed no other teaching; he was the son of Phalgunī, composed, his soul absorbed in yoga, and entirely devoted to yoga. 103.
He is the one to be known through yoga, the performer of yoga, the source of yoga, and the sky-clad one; his form is composed of the letters beginning with 'A' and ending with 'Kṣa'.
The Supreme Lord is praised as the lion with the mortar for a mouth; he has joined shanks, joined knees, joined palms, and wears a topknot. ||105||
Suśarman and Amitaśarman, who were devoted to Nārāyaṇa; Jiṣṇu, Bhaviṣṇu, Rociṣṇu, Grasiṣṇu, and Sthāṇu. ||106||
The tawny-hued one, the imitator of Rudra, the shaker of trees, the shaker of the earth, the flow of qualities, the inner thread of the self, free from passion, and fond of praise. 107.

He is the destroyer of the fear of the Naga maidens, golden-hued, and bearer of a skull; he is unperturbed, the means for attaining existence, free from decline, and one who has reached the further shore of the Vedas. ||108||
The imperishable Puruṣa, Lord of the world, the steadfast Protector and Master; he who enjoys the fruit of the eightfold yoga, who is true to his promise, and who is praised by many. ||109||

Dwelling in the cremation ground as his abode, capable of putting the spirits to flight, devoted to the five-syllabled mantra, the father of the five mothers, he whose banner is passion (Rañjana). 110.

He is the one to be saluted by the host of Yoginīs, the slayer of Śatrughna, possessed of infinite valor; he is the celibate student, the enemy of the senses, the wielder of the staff, and the ten-fold self. ||111||

He is free from conceptual proliferation, the one of noble conduct, the hero who pierces the army, the ancient one, supreme joy, bliss, the lord of the seven tongues of flame, and the sustainer. ||112||

The support of the city of nine gates, ever-fresh, the singer of the Sāman hymns, the abode of the six chakras, the celestial world, the giver of fearlessness, the bestower of honor, and free from intoxication. 113.

He who brings everything under his control, the power, the infinite one, the possessor of infinite auspiciousness; he who has eight forms, the sustainer, the leader, the multiformed, and the one beautiful with his own voice. 114.
Dhūmaketu, Mahāketu, Satyaketu, Mahāratha, Nandipriya, Svatantra, Mekhalin, and Samarapriya. ||115||
Lohāṅga, the all-knowing archer, the six-fold one, Śarva, Īśvara; the enjoyer of fruits, the one with fruit in hand, and the bestower of the fruits of all actions. ||116||
He is the overseer of dharma, the fruit of dharma, dharma itself, the bestower of dharma, and the giver of wealth; he knows the twenty-five principles and is devoted to the Tāraka Brahman. ||117||
The ground that abides in the three paths, the destroyer of all suffering, the vigorous, the partless, the wielder of the trident, the wearer of a garland, the roaring night-stalker. 118.
Clad in red garments, he is red in hue, adorned with a red garland; wearing a forest garland, his limbs are auspicious; and [another] is white, dressed in white garments, a youth.
Victory, victory to the one with his retinue, the thousand-faced sage, the destroyer of the hosts of Śākinīs, Ḍākinīs, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Bhūtas! ||120||
Sadyojāta, Kāmagati, Jñānamūrti, Yaśaskara, Śambhutejas, Sārvabhauma, Viṣṇubhakta, and Plavaṅgama. ||121||
The knower of ninety-four mantras, the destroyer of the pride of Rāvaṇa’s strength, the bestower of all prosperity, the glorious one, beloved of Aṅgada, and the praised one. 122.
Mindfulness is the seed; the Lord of the Gods is the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra; the Supreme is the retinue of Śrī; and Śrī, Bhū, Durgā, and Kāmākhyā [are the attendants]. (123)

He whose movement is constant, who is the wind, O Rāma; he who is a bee at the lotus-feet [of the Lord]; he who is fond of Nīla, who is blue in color, and who is a dear friend to those of blue complexion. ||124||
The messenger of Rāma, the friend of the world, the inner self, and the enchanting one; the hero who meditates upon Śrī Rāma and is always praised by the Kimpuruṣas. 125.
Rāma is the inner essence, purity, the goal, and humility; he is the one of virtuous fame, supreme bliss, the Supreme Lord, and the beloved charioteer. 126.
The Lord of the world, the giver of liberation, the cause of all causes; the one of great strength, the great hero, the teacher who has reached the further shore.
He is the witness of all the worlds and is worshipped by all the gods; he is firmly intent upon serving the feet of Śrī Rāma together with Sītā. 128.
Thus ends the hymn of a thousand names of Śrī Hanumān, who is steadfast in the service of the feet of Śrī Rāma accompanied by Śrī Sītā.
